narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Slightly warmer than yesterday; winds and cloud little changed. Showery from the afternoon, with thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. 29°C / 85°F high, 19°C / 66°F low. Sky mostly clear early as reported, mostly cloudy at midday and overcast in the evening. Wind SSW at midday; gusts to 36 km/h (19 kt). UV index 9.3 (very high). Air quality 83 (moderate) at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 20°C / 68°F; low so far 18°C / 64°F; peak sustained 15 km/h; sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with rain possible from Monday and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy Sunday, then partly cloudy Monday and Tuesday. Tuesday's call: rain, 57%, with two of four models wet; highs 28 to 31 °C. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it dry. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 80% of the time over 77 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Wednesday and Thursday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Friday and Saturday. Wednesday: all four models wet, highs around 30 °C. Thursday: all four models wet, the week's wettest day at 5 mm on average, highs much the same. Friday: two of three models wet, highs much the same, thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Thursday. ICON and UKMO are the wetter solutions from Wednesday to Thursday; GFS and ECMWF keep it drier. Saturday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 30 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 83% of the time over 73 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability today: UKMO 3150 J/kg, ECMWF 1940 J/kg, ICON 1180 J/kg and GFS 530 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 36 km/h (19 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 28 km/h (15 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1015 hPa) — a 7 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the south, southwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1015.0 and 1016.7 hPa, falling by 2.0 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: +0.2 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ECMWF first at Day+3, right 80% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 83% of the last 30 checks. On today's high ICON is the warmest model at 29.8 °C and UKMO the coolest at 27.4 °C; the call's 29.4 °C sits between them. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls a high of 29.0 °C and rain, agreeing with the call on rain. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest. At Day+0, Best Match slightly under-forecasts daytime highs here.

Figures issued 06:01. Written by code; a discussion follows when a model answers.
